facts.claim: The median company runs 34 experiments a year while top performers run more than 200
facts.source_title: Get more wins: experimentation metrics for program success
facts.excerpt: The median company runs 34 experiments a year, while top performers run 200+.

facts.claim: The median company runs two to three A/B tests a month
facts.source_title: Get more wins: experimentation metrics for program success
facts.excerpt: The median company runs 2 to 3 A/B tests per month.

facts.claim: A 12% win rate is the figure most often cited from large-scale analysis; a healthy band is 10% to 30%, on a conclusive rate of 35% to 40%
facts.excerpt: The most commonly cited win rate is 12%. A healthy win rate is 10 to 30%, with a healthy conclusive rate of 35 to 40%.

facts.claim: Impact per test peaks between one and ten tests a year per engineer, and past thirty the expected impact falls by 87%
facts.excerpt: Impact per test peaks at 1-10 annual tests per engineer. Beyond 30 annual tests per engineer, expected impact drops by 87%.

facts.claim: A survey of 206 companies places most organisations at the foundational or emerging stage of experimentation maturity
facts.excerpt: The VWO Experimentation Program Maturity Report, surveying 206 companies, finds the majority at foundational or emerging levels.

facts.claim: More than 300 teams run over 10,000 experiments a year across 750 million users in 186 markets, and 42% get rolled back after a guardrail metric flags a regression
facts.source_title: A/B test bandwidth: the currency of innovation
facts.excerpt: 300+ Spotify teams run 10,000+ experiments per year across 750 million users in 186 markets; 42% are rolled back after guardrail metrics flag a regression.

facts.claim: At a 5% baseline, detecting a 50% relative lift needs about 1,700 visitors per variant, a 20% lift about 9,000 and a 10% lift about 36,000
facts.source_title: Sample size calculation for A/B tests
facts.excerpt: A 5% baseline requires roughly 1,700 visitors per variant for a 50% relative lift, ~9,000 for 20% and ~36,000 for 10%.

facts.claim: Across 2,408 audited tests, 17.4% of A/B tests reached statistical significance with a winning variant
facts.source_title: A/B Test Win Rate: Benchmarks From 2,288 Audited Tests
facts.excerpt: 17.4% of A/B tests reached statistical significance with a winning variant across 2,408 tests.

facts.claim: Across 90-plus European e-commerce brands, 36.3% of tests produced a statistically significant win
facts.excerpt: 36.3% produced a statistically significant win across thousands of A/B tests on 90+ European e-commerce brands.

contradictions: Published A/B test win rates do not agree, and the gap is a definition gap rather than a performance one: optimizely.com cites 12% as the most common figure, conversionteam.com reports 17.4% reaching significance with a winning variant across 2,408 audited tests, and advertorialwizard.com reports 36.3% across 90-plus European e-commerce brands. The three differ on whether a win means statistical significance, a positive point estimate, or a shipped change. All three appear on this page with their definitions.
